title: Bus terminal check: corrected entry year

provenance.verification: Synthetic; checked by the team against its intended scenario before any run.
modifications: Subject first gives 2020 and corrects herself to 2019, explaining why; the officer records the correction.

narrative.text:
ENCOUNTER:
On February 14, 2024, at approximately 0640 hours, Border Patrol Agents [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] and [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] were performing transportation checks at the Greyhound bus terminal in Detroit, Michigan. Agent [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] identified himself and asked a passenger about her citizenship. The passenger, later identified as the subject, stated that she is a citizen of Guatemala and presented a Guatemalan passport. She stated that she did not have a visa or any other document allowing her to be in the United States. Agent [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] arrested the subject at approximately 0650 hours and transported her to the [REDACTED (b)(7)(E)] Border Patrol Station.

ENTRY:
The subject stated that she entered the United States on or about September 3, 2019, by wading across the Rio Grande near El Paso, Texas, and that she was not inspected by any immigration officer. She travelled by bus from El Paso to Chicago, Illinois, where she has lived since 2019.
When first asked, the subject said she entered in 2020. She then corrected herself and explained that she entered in September 2019, because her son was born in Chicago in December 2019, three months after she arrived. Agent [REDACTED (b)(6), (b)(7)(C)] recorded the entry as September 2019.
The subject is inadmissible under Section 212(a)(6)(A)(i) of the Immigration and Nationality Act, in that she is an alien present in the United States without being admitted or paroled.
DISPOSITION:
The subject was served a Notice to Appear and released on her own recognizance pending her hearing.
